meta.title: Walkback — Who called it—and who actually got it right?
meta.description: Sources make claims. Walkback checks them against Sui mainnet and demotes the ones that get it wrong.
meta.ogTitle: Walkback — Who called it—and who actually got it right?

common.disclaimer: Walkback audits public claims against onchain data. A low score means the claims we could check did not hold — not that the person is dishonest. Scores cover only the claims in this ledger, not the whole account.

nav.tagline: Who called it—and who actually got it right?

footer.record: Every claim, verdict and score version is written to Walrus Memory on mainnet.
footer.bound: Trust is a Wilson lower bound. A void is not a lie.

ingest.title: Turn a post into a receipt.
ingest.body: Walkback extracts claims that can be checked against Sui, freezes a balance snapshot at this moment, and writes each one to Walrus Memory. Most posts contain nothing checkable — that comes back as zero claims, not as an error.

memory.title: The ledger behind the ledger.
memory.body: Every claim, verdict and score version is written to Walrus Memory on mainnet. Walrus is the system of record; the Postgres tables the rest of the app reads are a rebuildable projection of it.
memory.verifyBody: Pages the relayer inventory and compares it with Postgres, record by record. Replacing the projection stays unavailable until every live product-namespace memory was read, the rebuild would not shrink any table, and no seed post is unfinished.

memory.empty: No memories in the projection yet. Ingest a post to write the first one.

method.title: Methodology
method.lead: How a stored claim is checked, and how a source gets a trust score. The rules on this page are the ones in the code.
method.typesBody:
Walkback stores a claim only when it can be checked. The closed set is a price forecast (price_threshold), a transaction check (tx_replay), a balance (balance_threshold), a balance change since ingest (balance_change_since_ingest), and manual.

A price forecast is checked against Tatum historical USD candles. A transaction check reads transfers with Tatum's Sui JSON-RPC method suix_queryTransactionBlocks and showBalanceChanges. A balance uses suix_getBalance. Sui has no historical balance query, so a change claim compares the snapshot taken at ingest with the balance at the deadline. A manual claim is always void: no automated check applies, and it never counts as a hit or a miss. Anything outside this set is rejected before it is stored.
method.priceBody:
A price claim is either a touch or a print at the deadline. A touch asks whether the price reached the target at any time from published_at up to, but not including, the deadline. A rise (gte) is compared with the candle high. A fall (lte) is compared with the candle low. The comparison uses the candle's unrounded decimal.

The read starts with daily USD candles. A daily candle whose whole bucket sits inside the window can establish the touch. If every overlapping daily high (a rise) or low (a fall) is short of the target, the claim is false and no finer candles are read. A daily candle that overlaps the window but is not fully inside it can only bound the overlap: its high or low may have printed outside. When that partial extreme reaches the target, or the edge of the window is missing, only that day is re-read hourly, and a boundary hour is re-read at one minute. If the finer series still cannot place the extreme inside the window, the claim could not be verified.

A deadline print (at_deadline) uses one candle that covers the deadline. The field is the close, or the open when the deadline is exactly the candle's open. If no evaluation was stored, the deadline print is what gets checked. The spot rate endpoint is not a verdict.
method.deadlinesBody:
When the post names a horizon, that horizon is the deadline, in UTC. Weeks run Monday through Sunday. This week ends that Sunday at 23:59:59.000Z. Next week ends the following Sunday. This week or next week ends the Sunday after next. This month, and by the end of a named month, end on that month's last day at 23:59:59.000Z.

A trade setup that states no date uses a benchmark of exactly 7 days after published_at. A technical-analysis post that states no date uses a benchmark of exactly 14 days. The deadline basis says that this is a benchmark convention. The six price claims collected on 2026-10-20 keep the deadlines chosen then, 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-08. They were not moved onto the 7-day or 14-day benchmark.

For a post ingested in the app, the model also resolves a relative deadline against the post time. “This week” published on a Tuesday means the following Sunday at 23:59 UTC. If it cannot resolve a deadline to an absolute timestamp, it drops the claim. The seed file already stores each deadline; those are not resolved again at display time.
method.conditionsBody: Some posts hedge the target, for example a breakout that could lead to a later price. The precondition is recorded and shown on the row. Adjudication judges the stored target. The condition does not change the verdict.
method.voidsBody: Void means the claim could not be verified. That happens when the deadline has not passed, there was no snapshot, the address is a placeholder, the claim is manual, the pair is not USD, the candle series does not cover the window, a boundary candle cannot place the extreme inside the window, the replay was truncated or a transfer could not be read, or the check failed. A void is not a miss. It does not count as a hit or a miss, and it does not move the score. A claim that was checkable and missed its target is false, and it stays in the ledger.
method.adjudicationBody: A model extracts claims. It is the only model call, and for a post ingested in the app it also resolves relative deadlines against the post time. It does not score them. Adjudication is rules over the stored parameters and the Tatum response. The trust score is the lower bound of a 95% Wilson score interval over hits and misses. It is not a raw hit rate and not a model call. One hit out of one claim is about 0.21. Eight out of ten is about 0.49.
method.bandsBody: The band name in the API is unknown, muted, normal, or trusted. Below 3 true or false verdicts in the record the feed uses, the band is unknown. This page says Not yet rated and shows an em dash with how many verdicts exist out of 3. That source is not hidden, even when a stored flag says otherwise. A bound below 0.40 has band muted. This page says Not passing verification, and those claims leave the default list. A bound of 0.55 or higher is trusted. Between the two cuts the band is normal.
method.categoriesBody:
Reporting counts transaction checks and both balance types. Forecasts count price claims. A manual claim is always void, so it never counts in the overall record or in either category.

The mute rule is forecast-primary. Any true or false price verdict selects the forecast record, including when that record is still under 3 and its band is unknown. Reporting is the record the feed uses only when there is no price verdict. A strong reporting record does not keep a weak forecaster in the list. One reporting miss does not hide a good forecaster. The homepage says which record the feed used, once that record has a verdict.
method.inclusionBody: Every claim that passes extraction is kept, whether it later comes out true, false, or could not be verified. The outcome is not a reason to drop or rewrite it. This ledger is not a random sample. Which posts are in it is decided by what gets ingested. The public set shipped with the repository is the retrospective benchmark in the seed file: 30 posts, 33 claims, 10 handles. Some candidates were left out on purpose, including one handle and both balance claims. The trust score does not adjust for how hard a call was. Extraction confidence is not an input to the Wilson bound. The samples are not independent. The eleven transaction checks from @_OnChainWatch were posted between 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-20. Four claims the collector scored below the 0.6 storage floor (cryptowithgopal 0.72, cryptowithgopal at or below 1, and both suintern_ posts) are stored at 0.6, as the seed file notes. Targets, windows, and wording are unchanged.
method.sourcesBody: Price checks use Tatum historical OHLCV: one candle from GET /v4/data/rate/symbol/OHLCV, or a page from the batch endpoint. Transaction and balance checks use Tatum's Sui mainnet JSON-RPC. The spot rate endpoint is not used as a verdict.
method.receiptsBody: Every claim, verdict, and score version is written to Walrus Memory on mainnet. The blob id is the receipt. This app does not invent a public URL for a blob. Memories are append-only: a correction is another memory, not an edit.
method.appealBody: If a stored claim, window, or verdict looks wrong, open an issue on the repository.
